– the failing test (signature + snippet),

– likely-relevant recent bug reports,

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test invokes PosixParser.parse on an Options object whose required options are set with OptionBuilder.isRequired().create("f") and "x". This causes a MissingOptionException with the message checked as "Missing required options: f, x".

The bug report states that from CLI 1.0 to 1.1, the MissingOptionException.getMessage() string format changed: previously options were prefixed with "-", now they are not, and the formatting is worse and less readable. The bug report hypothesizes that this change is due to Options.addOption no longer prefixing stored options with "-".

Inspecting Options.addOption(Option) shows that when adding an option, the key is obtained by opt.getKey() and this key is used to track required options in the requiredOpts list and the shortOpts map. The getKey() method returns opt if present, or longOpt otherwise. This means the keys stored do not have any "-" prefix added by Options.addOption.

From the test code, OptionBuilder.isRequired().create("f") creates an Option with opt = "f" (option short name), no leading "-". Thus, the `requiredOpts` list contains keys such as "f" and "x".

The MissingOptionException likely uses this stored requiredOpts list to generate its exception message listing missing options without any "-" prefix, causing the loss of clarity and formatting regressions observed in CLI 1.1, consistent with the bug report.

In CLI 1.0, it seems Options.addOption used to prefix the short option keys with "-", explaining the previous nicer and more readable message. This behavior is missing in the code snippet of CLI 1.1.

Hence, the bug arises because Options.addOption stores required options keys without "-" prefix, which propagate through to MissingOptionException message formatting, diverging from the expected output the test relies on.

This explains why the test expects "Missing required options: f, x" but the earlier CLI version expected "Missing required options: -f, -x" or similar, reflecting the missing "-" prefix in the message.

Fixing this issue would likely require restoring the prefixing of option keys with "-" when adding to required options or adjusting the message generation in MissingOptionException to format the option keys with "-" prefixes for clarity.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
